guide.factorycore.page.0:
Factory Guide

Build a storage network step by step. No scripts or other mods are needed for storage, hoppers or presets.

Turn the page to start.
guide.factorycore.page.1:
1. First network

Craft a Network Controller (4 iron, 4 redstone, 1 glass) and place it. It belongs to you. Connect blocks with Network Cable; controllers and cables join on all six faces.
guide.factorycore.page.2:
2. Storage

Craft a Storage Drive and a Starter Item Cell. Use the cell on the drive to install it (4 cells per drive). Cable the drive to the controller. Use the drive to see how full each cell is.
guide.factorycore.page.3:
3. Terminal

Place a Storage Terminal on the network and use it. Type to search. Left-click takes a stack; right-click takes half. Click with carried items to store them. Tabs show Fluids, Energy and Jobs.
guide.factorycore.page.4:
4. Hopper to terminal

Place a Buffered Interface on the network and point a hopper into it. It starts in Import when you place it, so hopper items appear in the terminal. Use it to see its contents and settings.
guide.factorycore.page.5:
5. Safe cell upgrades

Open the drive and click a cell's bay with a module on your cursor: Expansion, then Advanced, then Infinite. The cell stays in place and keeps its contents; failures cost nothing.
guide.factorycore.page.6:
6. Machines and presets

Put a Machine Interface against a machine and use it to set a label, resource, access, priority and rate. On Presets, pick Import, Export or Stock and press Apply: items move without any code.
guide.factorycore.page.7:
7. Power

Fuel Generators burn furnace fuel into FE. Energy Banks on the network store it. Programs, wireless blocks and links all run on FE.
guide.factorycore.page.8:
8. Crafting

Use the terminal grid to craft from storage and encode Blank Patterns. Put patterns in a Crafting Unit and request items in the Jobs view, or use Keep to hold stock.
guide.factorycore.page.9:
9. Processing

Processing Patterns go in a Crafting Interface facing a machine such as a furnace. Jobs send inputs and collect outputs automatically.
guide.factorycore.page.10:
10. Programs

A Program Controller runs simple rules such as keep 64 iron_ingot. Templates help you start. Advanced users can upload Wasm programs. It needs FE and Deploy rights.
guide.factorycore.page.11:
11. Branches

A Gateway's amber cross face is upstream (toward the controller) and its blue dot face is downstream (the branch). Use it to choose what the branch may do and see. Nested gateways only narrow access.
guide.factorycore.page.12:
12. Wireless

Power a Wireless Access Point, bind a Wireless Terminal to it and use the terminal within 64 blocks. Each action costs 64 FE from the handheld.
guide.factorycore.page.13:
13. Links

Place Wireless Link Endpoints against two gateways up to 256 blocks apart. Sneak-use one, then the other, to pair them. Each end needs its own FE.
guide.factorycore.page.14:
14. Progression

Starter: iron, copper, redstone, glass. Expanded: gold, quartz, ender pearls (Expansion Module, crafting, programs, gateways, wireless). Advanced: diamonds, ender eyes, netherite (Advanced Module, links). Infinite: a Nether star.
guide.factorycore.page.15:
15. Speed upgrades

Use Throughput on a port or buffer, then Overdrive. Use Overdrive on both link ends. Presets you deployed keep running. A busy server can still slow transfers. Capacity upgrades do not change speed.

command.factorycore.recovery.settle_scop: This record has its endpoint context; use /factorycore recovery return <id> instead. No transfer changed.

command.factorycore.recovery.port.adopte: Port %s adopted at %s, generation %s. Provider contents are unchanged; machine presets require authorized redeployment. Evidence: %s
command.factorycore.recovery.port.adopt_: Port adoption refused: match the canonical generation, load the old position without this port, select a stale nonfaulted holder of the same kind, and resolve uncertain transfers first. Nothing changed.
gui.factorycore.machine.window_first.hel: First slot or tank to use, counting from 0. Some machines cannot select tanks. Energy uses 0.
gui.factorycore.machine.window_count.hel: How many slots or tanks to use (1–64). For fluids, 0 or 64 uses every tank. Energy needs 64. Some machines need an exact slot range.
gui.factorycore.program.insert.help: Choose items, fluids, local labels or keywords without JEI. Ctrl+Space completes the cursor token. Ctrl+Z/Y undo/redo; Tab indents.
gui.factorycore.program.preview.help: Save and preview one native draft rule with your current View scope; repeat for the next rule. No transfers, reservations or FE charge. Escape returns to editing.
status.factorycore.buffer_reason.busy: Machine is in use by a crafting job; will retry when it finishes.
gui.factorycore.preset.status.busy: Machine is in use by a crafting job; will retry when it finishes.
gui.factorycore.terminal.job.reason.mach: Interface faces a different machine: restore its original orientation
gui.factorycore.terminal.job.reason.lega: Older dispatch has no proven target: cancel and inspect the original machine
gui.factorycore.terminal.job.reason.rese: Machine has a foreign hold or unresolved transfer: release or recover it first
gui.factorycore.terminal.job.reason.mach: This machine cannot be tracked by crafting jobs
The original machine is missing or was replaced: put it back
gui.factorycore.terminal.job.reason.lega: This older job cannot confirm its machine: cancel it and check the machine
message.factorycore.drive_installed: Cell installed in slot %s; routing awaits a valid network
gui.factorycore.drive.heading: %s · %s types
gui.factorycore.drive.bay.empty.help: Click with a cell on your cursor to install it in this bay, or Shift-click a cell in your inventory to fill the first empty bay.
gui.factorycore.drive.bay.full.help: Click to pick up this cell. Shift-click to send it to your inventory. Click with a module on your cursor to upgrade it here; its contents are kept.
gui.factorycore.drive.status.ready: Click a bay with a cell or a module on your cursor.
gui.factorycore.drive.status.wrong_item: Use a cell or an upgrade module on a bay
tooltip.factorycore.lamp_legend: Lamp: lit symbol = online · ! = needs attention · dark = idle
tooltip.factorycore.lamp_legend_program: Lamp: lit code = running · || = paused · ! = trapped or offline
tooltip.factorycore.network_controller.d: Root of one network. Connect cables to any face; use it to see network status and who has access.
tooltip.factorycore.gateway.description: Dot face is downstream (child branch), cross face upstream. Use it to see status and edit branch policy.
tooltip.factorycore.network_cable.descri: Joins devices into one network. Arms appear only toward faces that accept a connection.
tooltip.factorycore.storage_drive.descri: Holds four storage cells. Use it to see each cell and upgrade cells in place. An occupied bay shows a cell handle and lit lamp.
tooltip.factorycore.expansion_module.des: Click a Starter cell's drive bay with this module, or hold the cell or a bank in your offhand and use it. Upgrades to Expanded.
tooltip.factorycore.advanced_module.desc: Click an Expanded cell's drive bay with this module, or hold the cell or a bank in your offhand and use it. Upgrades to Advanced.
tooltip.factorycore.infinite_module.desc: Click an Advanced item cell's drive bay with this module, or hold the cell in your offhand and use it. Upgrades to Infinite.
tooltip.factorycore.blank_pattern.descri: Encode a crafting or processing recipe in the terminal's grid.
tooltip.factorycore.crafting_unit.descri: Runs crafting-table patterns placed in it for network crafting jobs.
tooltip.factorycore.crafting_interface.d: Front faces a machine; runs processing patterns through it.
tooltip.factorycore.program_controller.d: Runs one deployed program on its network. Use to open the editor; needs FE.
tooltip.factorycore.wireless_access_poin: Lets bound handheld terminals reach this network within range while powered.
tooltip.factorycore.wireless_link_endpoi: Place against a gateway, then sneak-use two endpoints to pair them. Needs FE.
tooltip.factorycore.factory_guide.descri: Use to read the in-game guide: first network, automation, crafting and upgrades.
tooltip.factorycore.throughput.advanced: Ports: %s items / %s mB / %s FE per tick. Buffers: %s items/tick.
tooltip.factorycore.throughput.endgame: After Throughput: ports %s items / %s mB / %s FE per tick; buffers %s items/tick. Both link ends: %sx pair limits.
tooltip.factorycore.throughput.install: Use on device: Edit rights; buffers also Deploy; links Manage. Failed use costs nothing. Links drop upgrades; other devices retain them.
tooltip.factorycore.throughput.fair: A busy server can still slow transfers; upgrades raise the device limit only.
tooltip.factorycore.throughput_unreadabl: Unrecognized device data: preserve it for recovery.
throughput.factorycore.server.throttled: busy (the server is limiting transfers; upgrades cannot help)
message.factorycore.throughput_status: Throughput: %s; up to %s %s each way; server load: %s
message.factorycore.link_throughput: Link throughput: %s; pair limit %s items, %s mB, %s FE per tick; server load: %s
message.factorycore.throughput_not_appli: This upgrade does not fit here (installed: %s). Order: Throughput, then Overdrive; links take only Overdrive.
message.factorycore.throughput_unknown_d: This device holds unsupported upgrade data; it is preserved for recovery.
message.factorycore.link_unknown_data: Unsupported link data is preserved; restore a compatible build or investigate the recovery item.
message.factorycore.throughput_denied: You need Edit (links: Manage) rights here to install an upgrade.
gui.factorycore.machine.status.upgrade: Rate exceeds the installed throughput upgrade; lower it or install an upgrade
gui.factorycore.gateway_policy.access.to: Open player access for this branch: grants, owner and the gateway limits that apply here
gui.factorycore.access.revoke.tooltip: Remove every explicit permission this player has on the network
gui.factorycore.access.make_owner.toolti: Transfer network ownership to this player (asks for confirmation)
gui.factorycore.access.recovery.tooltip: Inspect interrupted transfers and request safe cleanup
gui.factorycore.access.toggle.absent: %1$s: not granted to %2$s. Click to grant.
gui.factorycore.access.toggle.blocked: %1$s: granted to %2$s, but a gateway above blocks it here (*). Click to revoke.
gui.factorycore.access.owner_blocked: You own this network, but a gateway above blocks Manage here.
gui.factorycore.access.readonly: Read-only: you need Manage permission here.
gui.factorycore.access.root: Main network: no gateway limits apply here.
gui.factorycore.access.confirm_text: Transfer ownership of this whole network to %s? They get every permission. The current owner loses all access unless granted again. Other players' grants are kept.
gui.factorycore.access.empty: No players yet. Online players appear here so you can grant access.
gui.factorycore.access.readonly_help: Only the network owner, players with Manage and server operators can change access. Your own access and the gateway limits that apply here are shown above.
gui.factorycore.access.role.help: %s can: %s. Click for the next role: Guest views; Member also moves items and crafts; Builder also edits and deploys; Admin can do everything.
gui.factorycore.access.advanced.help: Switch between role buttons and the seven individual permission toggles.
gui.factorycore.access.status.denied: Access restricted: you need Manage here
gui.factorycore.access.status.owner: The owner already has every permission
gui.factorycore.access.status.unknown: That player is no longer listed
message.factorycore.access.transferred: %s transferred ownership of the Factory Core network at %s to %s.
gui.factorycore.recovery.return.tooltip: Send the items in transit back where they came from. A record is saved first; nothing is taken again.
gui.factorycore.recovery.settle.tooltip: Settle an older record that does not say where its items were going. A record is saved first.
gui.factorycore.recovery.retire.tooltip: Operators: archive a complete, empty record's evidence and remove it.
gui.factorycore.recovery.row.tooltip:
Record %s
State %s, %s %s
Delivered %s, returned %s, pending call %s
gui.factorycore.recovery.status.ready: Select a record to see its safe next step.
gui.factorycore.recovery.result: Cleanup step finished: %s. The record stays as evidence.
gui.factorycore.recovery.settled: Settlement step finished: %s. The record stays as evidence.
gui.factorycore.recovery.operator: Only server operators can retire records.
gui.factorycore.recovery.next.known: You started this transfer. Return sends the items in transit back where they came from; nothing is taken again.
gui.factorycore.recovery.next.known.othe: Items in transit. Only the player who started this transfer can return them; operators cannot.
gui.factorycore.recovery.next.legacy: Older record that does not say where its items were going. Settle returns them to their Factory Core source, or to a cell or bank you may deposit into.
gui.factorycore.recovery.next.legacy.oth: Older record that does not say where its items were going. Only the player who started it can settle it.
gui.factorycore.recovery.next.uncertain: This transfer could not be confirmed, so it is never repeated or refunded. Keep backups, check the container by hand and leave this record.
gui.factorycore.recovery.next.complete: Complete: kept as evidence. An operator may archive and retire it.
gui.factorycore.recovery.next.complete.o: Complete: kept as evidence. An operator may archive and retire it.

gui.factorycore.terminal.job.reason.unce: A machine call did not return: its outcome is unknown and is never retried; an operator must inspect the machine
gui.factorycore.terminal.job.reason.mach: Machine still records an earlier unfinished dispatch: an operator must inspect it with /factorycore recovery processing
